tagline: South from Why to the border, through the organ pipes.
intro: SR 85 leaves Why as a two-lane road and runs south into Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument, the only place in the country where the organ pipe cactus grows wild. The cactus keeps to rocky hillsides, out of the frost, and takes 150 years to come of age. Its white flowers open at night, for the bats, and close by morning.
The road was paved through to the border in 1942 and 1943, though it was not counted part of SR 85 until 1955. It ends at Lukeville, where the highway carries on into Mexico.

moments.title: Why
moments.text: Named for the Y where two highways once met. The story goes that place names needed three letters, so the founders spelled it out. The Y has since given way to a plain crossroads.

moments.title: Kris Eggle Visitor Center
moments.text: A tenth-mile nature trail starts at the visitor center, where the rare Quitobaquito pupfish can be seen among plenty of cacti.

moments.title: Lukeville
moments.text: A small border town with a post office and a duty-free shop, started by Charles Luke, brother of Frank Luke, the First World War flier.
